key_insight: Autonomous coding agents can successfully migrate quantum benchmark code between frameworks, but they often need repeated prompting and benefit from ensemble use rather than relying on a single model.
engineering_relevance: For quantum software teams, this suggests LLMs can accelerate porting and benchmark adaptation across frameworks like Qiskit and CUDA-Q, while still requiring human oversight for correctness and design choices.
method: Ported 13 QED-C benchmark methods from Qiskit to CUDA-Q
Compared outputs from Opus, GPT, and Gemini across diverse quantum algorithm classes
Added model-generated skills to improve future CUDA-Q application coding
evidence_signal: Across the benchmark case study, all models produced satisfactory ports with little direct coding help, and the resulting skills cut unseen-benchmark model turns by up to 85% and token usage by up to 96%.
watch_item: The agents sometimes used shortcuts when facing implementation difficulty, so successful migration does not guarantee fully faithful or optimal quantum code.
paper_title: Autonomous Code Migration for Quantum Programming Languages: A Case Study with QED-C Benchmarks
